ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: p(x) in the attached figure is a piecewise constant probability density function, and the horizontal axis marks -1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1. The PDF has height 1/3 on the outer intervals [-1,-0.5] and [0.5,1], and height 2/3 on the central interval [-0.5,0.5]. Reasoning calculation: 4-level uniform quantization covers [-1,1], so the quantization intervals are [-1,-0.5], [-0.5,0], [0,0.5], [0.5,1], the step size Δ=0.5, and the corresponding reconstruction levels are the midpoints of each interval, -0.75, -0.25, 0.25, 0.75. The signal power is E[x^2]=∫x^2p(x)dx. Using symmetry, the contribution of the two outer segments is 2*(1/3)*∫(0.5 to 1)x^2 dx = 7/36; the contribution of the central segment is (2/3)*∫(-0.5 to 0.5)x^2 dx = 1/18. Therefore E[x^2]=7/36+1/18=1/4. The quantization noise power is ∫(x-m_i)^2p(x)dx within each quantization interval. For each interval of width Δ=0.5, there is ∫(x-m_i)^2dx=Δ^3/12=1/96. The sum of the PDF heights of the four segments is 1/3+2/3+2/3+1/3=2, so the noise power is (1/96)*2=1/48. Therefore the linear quantization signal-to-noise ratio SQNR = (1/4)/(1/48)=12.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: identify the piecewise-constant PDF with heights 1/3 on the two outer half-intervals and 2/3 on the central interval. From the text, use 4-level uniform quantization, giving four intervals [-1,-0.5], [-0.5,0], [0,0.5], [0.5,1] and Δ=0.5. Compute signal power by integrating x^2p(x) over the three PDF regions, obtaining E[x^2]. Then compute quantization noise power by integrating (x-m_i)^2p(x) over each quantization interval, where m_i is that interval midpoint. Finally divide signal power by noise power to obtain the linear SQNR, which should evaluate to 12.
